visual.general_description: Hematoxylin and eosin stained microscopy field with a red erythrocyte-rich area and a purple cellular fragment.
visual.detailed_description: Light microscopy field without any printed text, scale bar, arrow or label. The upper and left parts are filled with densely packed red-pink round cells in a pale gray fibrillar background; a few isolated cells with dark blue-purple round nuclei are scattered in this area, and one larger round cell with a dark center and a pale halo lies left of the middle. The lower right part shows a blue-purple tissue fragment composed of crowded cells with elongated, dark, irregular nuclei and pale pink cytoplasm, crossed by a thin dark pink-purple vertical streak. A pink band is cut off at the upper right corner.

imaging_modalities.visual_cue: Light microscopy, FNA biopsy, hematoxylin and eosin stain

evidence.quote: FNA of the lesion revealed scattered and focal clusters of plasma cells with some crush artifacts (Figure 1).
At this point, a diagnosis of plasmablastic lymphoma was made.

visual.general_description: Immunohistochemical microscopy field with brown staining in a cell cluster and scattered brown granules.
visual.detailed_description: Light microscopy field without any printed text, scale bar, arrow or label. The lower left is occupied by a dense cluster with brown granular staining and pale blue counterstained nuclei, with several pale empty spaces inside it; a thin gray-brown curved band lies along its upper edge. The rest of the field above is a pale pinkish-white honeycomb-like background with many small scattered brown dots and granules and a few ring-shaped brown-rimmed round cells, one of which is at the top right corner.
